subject: Post-demo: ACME probe matrix & targeted hallucination tests
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice@acme.com>, Bob Carter <bob.carter@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 04 Oct 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: ACME probe matrix & targeted hallucination tests

Hi Alice / Bob,

Thanks again for your time today — great to walk through how Redwood would slot into ACME's doc ingestion pipeline and the latency profile you need for live support flows. As discussed, I put together a short probe plan to help your engineering and data science teams compare our inference behavior vs the hyperscaler you mentioned.

High-level asks from your side we captured on the call:
- Focus on hallucination rate on long-condition summaries (900-1,500 tokens).
- Evaluate prefix-cache impact on 95th pct latency.
- Verify behavior under burst load (20–40 concurrent chat sessions).

Attached: a starter probe matrix and a short prompt set focused on hallucination cases. The matrix maps tests to expected observables (BLEU/ROUGE not ideal here — we suggest targeted binary checks + human label buckets).

Next steps / Proposed owners:
1) ACME: pick 6 representative docs and 10 user prompts (we can help bootstrap) — owner: Alice
2) Redwood: run two side-by-side runs (your hyperscaler baseline vs Redwood-hosted instance) and return unified CSV of outputs + token-latency breakdown — owner: Marissa
3) Joint: schedule a 60-min triage to review divergences; if we see >5% hallucination delta we’ll dig into prompt-sensitivity and propose mitigations (temperature, retrieval-k, model variant) — owner: Rishi + ACME eng reps

Proposed schedule:
- ACME to share doc samples by Thu 10/07
- Redwood returns run results by Tue 10/12
- Triage meeting Wed 10/13 (30–60 min)

Let me know if that timeline looks OK and whether to include anyone else from ACME’s side.

Thanks,

— Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
[Attachment: acme-probe-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet, 24 KB)]
[Attachment: hallucination-sample-prompts.txt (text, 4 KB)]

-----
From: Alice Nguyen <alice@acme.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Bob Carter <bob.carter@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 04 Oct 2027 16:04:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: ACME probe matrix & targeted hallucination tests

Thanks Stephanie — this looks actionable. A couple quick clarifications:

1) For the long-condition summaries, we mainly care about omission hallucinations (critical facts dropped) over addition hallucinations. Is the matrix set up to separate those buckets?
2) On burst load, our current constraints are 35 concurrent sessions sustained for ~5 minutes. We’d like to see both sustained and spike (10s) patterns.

We’ll pull 6 docs and have them to you by end of day Thu (10/07). Can Marissa confirm the CSV schema you expect so our data folks can align?

Best,
Alice
Alice Nguyen
Senior ML Eng, ACME Corp
alice@acme.com

-----
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice@acme.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 05 Oct 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: ACME probe matrix & targeted hallucination tests

Hi Alice — thanks, and good point on omission vs addition. The probe matrix has separate rows for the two types; the sample prompts file also flags the expected truth spans so the human labelers can mark omission vs fabrication easily.

CSV schema (what we’ll deliver):
- test_id
- prompt_text
- doc_id
- baseline_output (hyperscaler)
- redwood_output
- baseline_tokens_total
- redwood_tokens_total
- baseline_mean_latency_ms
- redwood_mean_latency_ms
- baseline_p95_latency_ms
- redwood_p95_latency_ms
- omission_flag (0/1)
- addition_flag (0/1)
- human_label_notes

We’ll also include a simple summary sheet with per-test pass/fail under your acceptance criteria (you can define thresholds — default we'll use 5% delta on hallucination rate and 10% p95 latency delta).

On bursts: we’ll run two profiles: sustained 35 clients for 5 minutes and spike profile with 10s bursts at 120 req/s. We’ll surface token-level CPU/GPU utilization and KV cache hit rates where applicable.

Deliverables timeline reiterated:
- Thu 10/07: ACME supplies docs + acceptance thresholds
- Tue 10/12: Redwood delivers CSV + summary + raw outputs
- Wed 10/13: Triage call 09:00 PT (I’ll send calendar invite once times look good)

Let us know if you want the raw transcript logs (we can provide sanitized ones) — they’re helpful for root-cause in hallucination cases.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
[Attachment: sample-csv-schema.csv (text, 2 KB)]

-----
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alice Nguyen <alice@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 06 Oct 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Post-demo: ACME probe matrix & targeted hallucination tests

Looping in Aditya to confirm config choices for the baseline runs — Aditya, can you run the Redwood-hosted tests with the following initial config so we have apples-to-apples with ACME’s hyperscaler baseline?

- Model variant: rwd-1.3-medium (float16, no quant)
- Temp: 0.2 (but we’ll include 0.0 / 0.5 in ablations)
- Retrieval k: 3 (when doc context exists)
- Batch policy: continuous batching, max batch size 64, latency SLO 200 ms
- KV cache warm start for long-condition tests (preload doc shards)

Aditya — also capture token-level p95 and a 2-minute window of GPU utilization during sustained 35-client profile. Save the raw outputs in the linked Drive folder and tag filenames with test_id.

Thanks — I’ll draft the invite once ACME confirms times.

Rishi
Head of Applied ML, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

[Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C-acme-probes]
